title: Optical characterization of excited-state spin Hamiltonians and clock transitions at telecommunication wavelength in Tm3+:YAlO3
authors: Akshay Babu Karyath, Luozhen Li, Julien Bertrand, Alexandre Kings, Tianyang Shen, Gabriel Aeppli, Simon Gerber, Guy Matmon, Wolfgang Tittel
abstract: The zero-phonon line (ZPL) between the two excited-state manifolds 3F4 and 3H4 of the trivalent thulium ion in yttrium aluminum perovskite (Tm3+:YAlO3) lies within the telecom E-band at around 1451 nm and exhibits an optical coherence time of a few μs at cryogenic temperatures. To improve this time in view of potential applications, e.g. single-photon sources and optical quantum memory, we characterized the magnetic properties of the lowest Stark levels of these two manifolds. Varying the external magnetic field amplitude and orientation, we measured the enhanced nuclear Zeeman splitting by probing the field-dependent frequency detuning of side holes created by means of spectral hole burning, and we characterized the inhomogeneous line shift caused by the quadratic Zeeman interaction. Together, this allowed us to establish the spin Hamiltonians for the lowest Stark level of the 3F4 and 3H4 manifolds, and to predict optical clock transitions for particular orientations and magnitudes of the magnetic field
summary: This experimental study characterizes the magnetic spin Hamiltonians of $	ext{Tm}^{3+}$ ions in $	ext{YAlO}_3$ using high-resolution spectroscopy at telecom wavelengths. By measuring field-dependent spectral splittings, the authors quantified the effects of the nuclear and electron Zeeman interactions. The results enable the prediction of stable optical clock transitions, advancing the use of these materials for quantum information applications.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the magnetic properties of the lowest Stark levels of the $3F_4$ and $3H_4$ excited-state manifolds of $	ext{Tm}^{3+}$ in $	ext{YAlO}_3$ to establish their spin Hamiltonians.
main_result: The authors successfully determined the spin Hamiltonians by measuring field-dependent splittings (enhanced nuclear Zeeman effect) and quadratic shifts, allowing them to predict specific optical clock transitions.
method: Measurements were performed using spectral hole burning on the $1451 	ext{ nm}$ Zero-Phonon Line (ZPL) while applying controlled external magnetic fields up to $2 	ext{ T}$.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Tm}^{3+}$ ions in $	ext{YAlO}_3$, analyzed using a generalized spin Hamiltonian incorporating hyperfine, Zeeman, and crystal-field interactions. The analysis focuses on the $	ext{Y1} \leftrightarrow 	ext{X1}$ transition between the $3H_4$ and $3F_4$ manifolds.
key_observables: Frequency detuning of side holes, inhomogeneous line shift (quadratic Zeeman effect), and the magnetic field dependence of these shifts.
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperatures ($\sim 800 	ext{ mK}$), magnetic fields up to $2 	ext{ T}$, and the telecom E-band wavelength ($\sim 1451 	ext{ nm}$).
main_assumptions: The determination of the Hamiltonian relies on fitting measured splittings to theoretical models, and the estimation of coherence time ($	ext{T}_2$) using the Hessian matrix provides only a lower bound.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level diagrams showing transitions, the magnetic field coordinate system relative to crystal axes, and spectral hole profiles demonstrating central and side-hole splittings.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical context and the general Hamiltonian, through detailed measurements of Zeeman splittings and quadratic shifts using spectral hole burning, culminating in the derivation of the spin Hamiltonians and the prediction of clock transition points.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses precise spectroscopic techniques to map out the fundamental quantum mechanical interactions (hyperfine, Zeeman) governing rare-earth ion energy levels, which is crucial for developing solid-state quantum memories and quantum sensors.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Energy level diagram of Tm3+:YAlO3 where 3H6 is the ground-state manifold ; 3F4 and 3H4 are excited-state manifolds. At right, a schematic of the evolution of the lowest Stark levels of the 3F4 and 3H4 manifolds (Y1 and X1, respectively) with applied magnetic field. Each level shifts quadratically (dashed line, due to the quadratic Zeeman shift) and splits linearly into two nuclear-spin sublevels (solid line, caused by the enhanced nuclear Zeeman effect), with total splittings δeX1 and δeY1, respectively. |↑⟩and |↓⟩denotes the nuclear spin states. Energy axes not to scale.

FIG. 2. Definition of the magnetic-field coordinate system relative to the crystal axes (a, b, c) of Tm3+:YAlO3. The magnetic field B is parametrized by the polar angle θ, mea- sured with respect to the c axis and the azimuthal angle ϕ, measured in the ab plane with respect to the a axis. The gray box indicates the cut of the Tm3+:YAlO3 crystal.

FIG. 3. Spectral holes of the 1451 nm Y1-X1 transition at T=0.92 K with an applied magnetic field of 2 T oriented along the b-axis of the crystal. The figure shows a central hole at zero detuning together with four side holes located symmetri- cally about it, which arise from the inhomogeneous broaden- ing of the transition along with atomic level splittings. When B ∥b, the detunings of the inner pair (blue dotted lines) and the outer pair (red dotted lines) correspond to the enhanced nuclear Zeeman splittings δeY1 and δeX1 of the Y1 and X1 levels, respectively.

FIG. 4. Angular dependence of the enhanced nuclear Zeeman splitting rate for the X1 level of the 3H4 manifold and the Y1 level of the 3F4 manifold of Tm3+:YAlO3. Top row (a)-(c): X1; bottom row (d)-(f): Y1. For B within the ab plane (panels (a),(d)) site 1 and site 2 are magnetically inequivalent, resulting in distinct splittings (blue circles, site 1; orange squares, site 2), whereas for B within the bc and ac planes (panels (b),(e) and (c),(f), respectively), the sites are magnetically equivalent and yield the same splittings. Markers depict measured data; solid lines are fits using Eq. (8). Radial axis: splitting rate in MHz/T. The procedure for assigning measurements to site 1 and site...

FIG. 5. Detuning of the center of the inhomogeneous broad- ened line of the excited-state transition (Y1 - X1) as a func- tion of magnetic field amplitude, for B oriented along the three crystal axes of Tm3+:YAlO3. Each set of data is fitted with a quadratic function ∆ν = ki · B2 (i=a,b,c), after sub- tracting the zero-field (B = 0 T) baseline detuning. The fitted quadratic shift rates ∆ki are indicated, including uncertain- ties. The error bars of the individual data points characterize the uncertainty with which the center of the inhomogeneous absorption line could be established.
